data.name: Dwaipayan
data.gender_notes: Dwaipayan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Dwaipayan is derived from the Sanskrit words ‘dwai’ meaning two and ‘payan’ meaning boats or islands. In Hindu mythology, Dwaipayan is an epithet given to sage Vyasa, the author of the Mahabharata. Vyasa is believed to have composed the epic on two islands, Badri and Shankhachudamani. The name Dwaipayan carries the meaning “Two boats or islands” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Dwaipayan usually hope their child will grow to embody two boats or islands and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Dwaipayan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Two boats or islands.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dwaipayan total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: Dwaipayan is a evocative name that highlights the legendary journey of one of the greatest sages in Hinduism, sage Vyasa, who authored the Mahabharata on two islands. This name carries the rich cultural heritage of Indian epic literature and inspires curiosity about the intriguing tales and vast knowledge contained within the Mahabharata.
data.spiritual_significance: Dwaipayan as a name holds significant spiritual symbolism in Hinduism. It signifies the unwavering devotion, determination, and divinity of Sage Vyasa, who dedicated himself to recording the Hindu wisdom and knowledge to preserve it for generations to come. The name also emphasizes the harmony and unity of the physical and spiritual worlds, as Vyasa composed the epic on two islands, linking the realms of humanity and divinity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Dwaipayan, meaning 'two boats', signifies the dual journey of life - the physical and the spiritual. It represents the continuous effort to navigate through both worlds, balancing material and spiritual growth.
